title: Trace when the resource closes, the catch runs and finally runs

blocks.text: A try-with-resources statement can carry `catch` and `finally` blocks, as in the page's syntax example. The resources are closed as the `try` block exits, before any `catch` or `finally` block of the same statement runs.
Write `Traced.run(Opener opener, Body body, List<String> log)` as one try-with-resources statement with a `catch` and a `finally`:

items: declare the resource `opener.open("r")` (the opener and the resource record `"open r"` and `"close r"` in the same log themselves);
catch any `IOException` (from opening, from the body or from closing) and add `"caught " + message`; anything else leaves `run` unchanged, after the steps below;

rows: `open r, body done, close r, finally`

blocks.text: Work out where `"caught boom"` lands when the body throws `IOException("boom")`, and which block handles a failure of the resource's own `close()`.

cases.says: A clean run opens, runs the body, closes the resource, then runs finally.
When the body throws, the resource is closed before the catch block runs.
A failure while closing the resource is caught by the statement's own catch block.
Only an IOException is caught; an unchecked failure leaves the method, after the resource is closed and the finally block has run.
A failure to open the resource is caught by the statement's own catch, and finally still runs.

concepts: A catch or finally block of a try-with-resources statement runs after its resources are closed, and it also sees close failures.
